findings.description: SPEC AMBIGUITY ON THE EXACT GOOGLEFINANCE CALL, surfaced by both directions. SHEET-MARK-008 says only that the formula 'encodes GOOGLEFINANCE's trade date' — it never names the literal attribute string. The real formula (lib.rs:270-274) is `=IFERROR(TEXT(INT(GOOGLEFINANCE("{ticker}","tradetime"))-DATE(1970,1,1),"0"),"")` — using the `"tradetime"` attribute (a datetime serial) and an `INT()` truncation to strip time-of-day before rebasing. Given the EARS text ALONE, 2 of 3 A-runs (A2, A3) independently guessed `"tradetime"` + `INT()` correctly, but A1 read 'trade date' literally and invented `GOOGLEFINANCE(symbol,"tradedate")` — an attribute that does not exist in Google Sheets — with no INT() truncation at all. That formula would not evaluate against the real API. On the B side, all three runs independently reconstruct 'tradetime' and 'INT(...)' as pinned, load-bearing constants (formula.rs's test literally asserts the rendered formula text contains the substring "tradetime"), confirming this is a magic string the spec text never states verbatim yet the implementation and its tests hard-depend on getting exactly right.

SILENT DEFAULT-TO-EPOCH ON MALFORMED/ABSENT QUOTE DATE, unstated by the spec, and a point of real A-run disagreement. SHEET-MARK-008 says nothing about what happens if the read-back Quote Date cell is missing or fails to parse. The real code (adapters.rs:314-323, `price_reading_from_cells`) parses column 12 with `.and_then(|s| s.trim().parse::<i32>().ok()).unwrap_or(0)` — ANY non-numeric or absent cell (a still-loading formula, a broken formula, a short row) silently becomes `Date(0)` (1970-01-01), a value indistinguishable from a genuine epoch-0 quote date, folded straight into an otherwise-valid `PriceReading::Numeric`. All three B-runs independently pin this exact fallback ('default `quote_date` to `Date(0)`/`0` rather than failing the row or propagating an error' — B1 item 10, B2 item 9, B3's unwanted-behavior clause). The A-runs, having no code to observe, diverge sharply on this exact question: A1 and A2 treat malformed non-empty content the same as empty (silently `None`), while A3 explicitly designs a hard `Result::Err(QuoteDateParseError::NotAnInteger)` for the same case — the opposite of the real code's silent, undetectable fallback. The spec's total silence on this directly produces incompatible A-side inventions, one of which (A3) actively contradicts the real code's error-swallowing contract.

HARD-CODED, HEADER-INDEPENDENT COLUMN POSITIONS not stated anywhere in the EARS. The real read-back (adapters.rs:299-300) fixes `const PRICE_COL: usize = 4; const QUOTE_DATE_COL: usize = 12;` — magic numeric offsets into the raw grid, with no header-name lookup; formula.rs separately hard-asserts `qcol == 12` on the Positions header. The EARS text is entirely position-agnostic — it never says the settle pass reads by fixed column index rather than by header name, and never says a Positions-header reorder is unsupported. All three B-runs converge tightly on this exact pinned pair of constants (PRICE_COL=4 / QUOTE_DATE_COL=12) and its 'fixed offset, not searched by header' character (B3), meaning any future Positions-column reordering would silently misread the wrong cell as the quote-date stamp rather than erroring. None of the three A-runs touch tab column position at all; A2 explicitly defers 'header text/column placement' as 'outside this sketch's scope,' so this is a pure code-side surplus with no A-side counterpart.

QUOTE-DATE CONSULTATION IS GATED ENTIRELY ON THE PRICE CELL BEING NUMERIC — an implementation-only linkage the EARS never states. In the real `price_reading_from_cells`, column 12 is parsed ONLY inside the `Ok(price_usd) =>` match arm (adapters.rs:314-323); if the Price cell (col 4) is empty, 'Loading...', '#N/A', or any other leading-'#' error, the function returns `Transient`/`Permanent` and the Quote Date cell is never even looked at. SHEET-MARK-008 describes the Quote Date column and its parsing as its own independent concern with no mention of this Price-state gate. All three B-runs state the gating explicitly (B1 item 11, B2 item 10, B3's closing ubiquitous clause: 'a non-numeric Price reading carries no quote-date value at all'). None of the three A-runs model this relationship — each treats the parser as a standalone function with no dependency on a sibling Price reading, since the spec gives no reason to invent that coupling from EARS text alone.

notes: The three A-runs agree tightly on overall shape (IFERROR-wrap to \"\", DATE(1970,1,1) rebasing, TEXT(...,\"0\") digits-only rendering, treating the parsed result as a bare epoch-day integer) — genuinely spec-traced behavior matching the real code closely. Where they diverge is exactly where the EARS text is silent or ambiguous: the literal GOOGLEFINANCE attribute name (2/3 'tradetime' vs 1/3 'tradedate', a nonexistent attribute) and malformed-value handling (2/3 silent None vs 1/3 hard Err) — hence 'medium' A-agreement rather than 'high'. All three A-runs also unanimously chose i64 for the epoch-day type where the real kernel Date wraps i32; per the classification rules this unanimous, spec-unbased invention is an assumption artifact, not a finding, so it is omitted from the findings list. The three B-runs are extremely tight: near-verbatim formula string reconstruction, identical PRICE_COL=4/QUOTE_DATE_COL=12 constants, identical silent-default-to-0 fallback, identical Price-numeric gating, and identical claim that the aliased/resolved ticker (not the bare symbol) is what the formula must contain — hence 'high' B-agreement. Real files consulted: crates/sheets-view/src/lib.rs (quote_date_formula, render_positions, PriceReading, POSITIONS_HEADER), crates/runtime/src/adapters.rs (price_reading_from_cells, PRICE_COL/QUOTE_DATE_COL), crates/sheets-view/tests/formula.rs (positions_carries_a_locale_proof_quote_date_companion_column).
